subject: science

entries: The loop: battery, bulb and ammeter joined by wires form one unbroken loop - the battery pushes charge around it, the bulb turns electrical energy into light, and the ammeter measures the flow.
slots.label: The loop
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Direction: conventional current leaves the positive terminal, crawls around the loop, and returns to the negative terminal - follow the red markers.
slots.label: Direction
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Paths: in series there is one path and one broken bulb kills the loop; in parallel each bulb has its own branch, so one can fail and the other stays lit.
slots.label: Paths
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Ohm's law: with resistance fixed at 4 ohms, stepping the battery from 6 to 12 volts speeds the markers up and climbs the ammeter from 1.5 to 3 amps - 12 divided by 4 is 3.
slots.label: Ohm's law
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Not used up: ammeters before and after the bulb in a series loop both read 0.5 amps - the bulb changes energy's form, not the current's size.
slots.label: Not used up
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Summary: current flows positive to negative around a single loop, series means one path while parallel means many, and the series current is identical everywhere under V = I R.
slots.label: Summary
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: One unbroken loop of components joined by wires, around which charge flows; break the loop anywhere and the flow stops everywhere.
slots.label: Circuit
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The flow of charge around the loop, measured in amps by an ammeter; in a series loop it is the same at every point.
slots.label: Current
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The agreed direction of current flow: out of the battery's positive terminal, around the loop, and back into the negative terminal.
slots.label: Conventional current
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An arrangement with only one path for the charge, so every component carries the same current and one break stops everything.
slots.label: Series
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An arrangement where each component sits on its own branch, so one can fail while the others keep working.
slots.label: Parallel
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms; in Ohm's law, V = I R, a fixed 4 ohm resistance lets 12 volts drive 3 amps.
slots.label: Resistance
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The relation V = I R between voltage, current and resistance: with resistance fixed, doubling the voltage doubles the current.
slots.label: Ohm's law
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The unit of current: the series loop in the animation carries 0.5 amps, read the same on both sides of the bulb.
slots.label: Amp
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: Electricity: circuits, current and Ohm's law
